subject: Transportation Systems
title: Port Automation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Port Automation usable.

hook.text: Rotterdam's newest terminal operates almost without people. Cranes, trucks, and stackers are robotic.

buildup.text: Automated stacking cranes sort containers in the yard by destination, weight, and departure time.

discovery.text: Computer systems decide where every container sits—optimizing space and retrieval speed.

twist.text: Automation slashes labor costs but faces fierce union opposition in many countries.

climax.text: Fully automated ports handle more volume with fewer errors—but they need years of software tuning.

punchline.text: The port of the future has cranes but no crane operators.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of port automation?
options: Higher volume handled with fewer errors and lower labor costs
